visual: Compact variegated shrub with silvery-white and green foliage. New growth is attractively flushed pink, with fragrant white to pale pink tubular flowers produced over a long flowering season.
water: Water regularly while establishing. Once established, water during prolonged dry periods; relatively drought tolerant.
aspect: Full sun; sheltered south- or west-facing position preferred
soil: Fertile, well-drained chalk, loam or sandy soil; tolerant of acid, neutral or alkaline conditions.
soilWarning: Avoid waterlogged soil and cold, exposed positions. Good light encourages the strongest variegation and flowering.
prune: Lightly prune after flowering to maintain a compact shape and remove damaged or unwanted growth. Older plants can be renovated by removing some older stems.
hardinessNote: Hardy in most UK locations, approximately -15 to -10°C, but benefits from shelter in colder or exposed areas.
resilience: Generally robust and relatively drought tolerant once established, but performs best in a warm sheltered position.
uses: Sunny borders, patio containers, courtyard gardens, low informal hedging and wall-side planting.
foliage: Semi-evergreen; small green leaves broadly variegated creamy to silvery white, with attractive pink flushing on young and seasonally coloured growth.
container: Excellent compact shrub for a large container in a sunny, sheltered position.
uncertain: RHS lists Linnaea × grandiflora 'Sparkling Silver' as a synonym and currently treats the cultivar name status as unresolved.
